tools.description: Claim a frame before working in it, so other agents cannot change it while you do. The claim lapses after 60 seconds without a change from you, and a person can always edit or stop it. Claim fails when another agent holds the frame; pick another one or wait.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

tools.name: claim_frame

tools.description: Copy layers, with everything inside them, to a page or layer. Copies get new ids, returned in the order of `copies`. One change for the whole batch.

copies.description: What to copy and where each copy goes.

index.description: Where among the parent's children, back to front. Defaults to the top (the end).

parent.description: The page or layer it goes into, by id.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

tools.name: copy_nodes

tools.description: Make layers into components: each layer's tree becomes a component definition and the layer becomes its first instance. Returns the component ids in order; use create_instance to place more.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

ids.description: The layers to make into components. Each stays where it is, as the first instance of its component.

tools.name: create_component

tools.description: Place instances of local components, with their props and overrides. Each is sized like its component unless `set` says otherwise. Returns the new ids in order, as one change.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

component.description: The local component, by id (list_components shows them).

index.description: Where among the parent's children, back to front. Defaults to the top (the end).

parent.description: The page or layer it goes into, by id.

set.description:
Instance properties in the file format: `name`, `position`, `width`, `props` (the component's props by
name), `overrides`. Size and name default to the component's.

tools.name: create_instance

tools.description: Remove layers and everything inside them, as one change. The person can undo it; still, read what you are removing first.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

ids.description: The layers to remove, each with everything inside it.

tools.name: delete_nodes

tools.description: Run a short JavaScript program against the document's `doc` API: loops and variables do in one call what would take many tool calls. The whole script is one change and one undo step; if any call fails, nothing is applied and the error names the line. `validate_only` reports what would change. Limits: 5 seconds, 2,000 calls, 2,000 new layers; no network, files or timers.

code.description:
A JavaScript program using `doc` (read_skill "execute" documents it): doc.page, get, query, insert,
update, copy, replace, move, delete, setVariables, createComponent, makeSlot, instance, findSpace,
layoutProblems, screenshot, export, claim, release. `return` a value to get it back; return
doc.screenshot(id) to see the result.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

validate_only.description: Run it and report what would change, without changing anything.

tools.name: execute

tools.description: List every distinct value a property takes in a scope, with how many nodes have each and a few example ids. Use it to see what a design already uses (font sizes, colours, radii) before adding more, or to find values that should be a variable. Variable references show as {"$var": id}.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

limit.description: The most distinct values to list (default 100, at most 500).

property.description:
The property, in the file's spelling, with dots into nested objects. Lists are looked through, so
`content.size` is every text run's size and `fills.color` is every fill colour. Examples: `cornerRadius`,
`gap`, `content.font`, `stroke.width`.

scope.description: Only look inside this page, component or node.

tools.name: find_properties

tools.description: Find an empty area of the canvas of a given size, clear of every frame already on the page. Use it to place a new top-level frame instead of guessing coordinates. Returns the rectangle.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

height.description: The height of the area needed.

near.description: Prefer the free area nearest this point.

page.description: The page to look on. Defaults to the first page.

width.description: The width of the area needed.

tools.name: find_space

tools.description: Report what is open and what the person sees: open documents, the active one, its selection and viewport, which frames are leased (and by which agent; `you` is this client's), which agents are paused, and the notes for agents and context nodes that apply to the selection (or the page, with no selection). Call it first, and again before starting on a new request.

document.description: The document whose selection, leases and notes to report. Defaults to the active document.

tools.name: get_app_state

tools.description: Read nodes by id, with their children down to `depth`. Use it to look at a frame before changing it. Children past the depth are counted in `childCount`; nodes past `max_nodes` come back as stubs.

depth.description:
How many levels of children to include: 0 is the node alone with a `childCount`, 1 (the default) adds
its children. At most 8.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

ids.description: The ids of the nodes to read. Page ids are not nodes; use query_nodes with `scope` to list a page.

max_nodes.description:
Stop after this many nodes in all (default 300, at most 2000). Nodes past it come back as stubs with
`truncated: true`.

tools.name: get_nodes

tools.description: List the document's variables (colours, numbers, strings, booleans) and its theme axes. Each shows its id, name and type, the value it has under the theme, and every value it can take. Bind a property to a variable with {"$var": id}; prefer a variable over a literal that matches one.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

name.description: Only variables whose name contains this, ignoring case.

theme.description: Theme axis values to resolve under, such as {"Mode": "dark"}. Axes left out take their first value.

tools.name: get_variables

tools.description: Add nodes (with their children) to a page or a layer, as JSON or as a compact tag spec. All of them go in as one change, or none do. Returns the new top-level ids in order. A mistake is reported with the index and field of the node to fix.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

index.description: Where among the parent's children, back to front: 0 is the bottom. Defaults to the top (the end).

nodes.description: The nodes, in the file format (see read_skill). `id` and `name` may be left out; children nest.

parent.description: The page or layer to add them to, by id.

spec.description:
The nodes as text instead, in `format`. With "jsx" (the default) a tag is a node's type, attributes are
its properties ("text" or {json}), nested tags are children and text inside <text> is its content:
<frame name="Card" width={320} height="hug" layout="column"><text font="Inter" size={14}>Hi</text></frame>

tools.name: insert_nodes

tools.description: List the document's components: id, name, root node, the props an instance can set, the variants, the slots that accept other components, and how many instances use each. Use a component instead of drawing the same thing again.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

name.description: Only components whose name contains this, ignoring case.

tools.name: list_components

tools.description: List the fonts text can use: the families the engine can draw, the fonts stored in this document, and the families its text already uses. A text run names a family; one that is not listed is drawn with a fallback and looks different from what you asked for.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

tools.name: list_fonts

tools.description: Mark empty frames inside a component as slots, which each instance fills with its own content. Suggest the components that usually go there. One change for the batch.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

slots.description: The frames to make into slots.

id.description: An empty frame inside a component definition (not its root).

suggested.description: Components suggested for the slot, by id. Advisory: anything can fill it.

tools.name: make_slot

tools.description: Move layers to another parent or page, or to another place among their siblings. A layer cannot move into itself or between a page and a component. One change for the whole batch.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

moves.description: What moves where, in order. An index counts the parent's children after the layer has left its old place.

index.description: Where among the parent's children, back to front. Defaults to the top (the end).

parent.description: The page or layer it goes into, by id.

tools.name: move_nodes

tools.description: Open a .vellum document, or create it with `create: true`. If an editor has the file open, work happens in that editor; otherwise the file is opened without one. Returns the pages. Calls that leave out `document` use the document opened last.

create.description: Make the file when it is not there. An existing file is opened, never replaced.

name.description: The name for a new document. Defaults to the file name.

path.description: The path of the .vellum file, relative to the repo.

tools.name: open_document

tools.description: Find nodes by name, type, text, component or variable use, optionally inside one page or node. Returns short summaries in reading order; use get_nodes for the detail. All filters given must match.

component.description: Only instances of this component, by component id.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

limit.description: The most nodes to list (default 50, at most 500). `total` is the full count.

name.description: Only nodes whose name contains this, ignoring case.

scope.description: Only look inside this page, component or node.

text.description: Only text, notes and prompts whose characters contain this, ignoring case.

variable.description: Only nodes that use this variable, by variable id or exact name.

tools.name: query_nodes

tools.description: Let go of a frame you claimed, when you are done with it, so other agents can work there.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

tools.name: release_frame

tools.description: Remove layers and put new ones in exactly their place in the layer order. Use it to swap a layer for a different kind of layer; to change properties use update_nodes. Returns the new ids.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

replacements.description: The layers and what replaces each.

node.description: What goes in its place, in the file format. It may keep the old id.

tools.name: replace_nodes

tools.description: Change every use of one value of a property to another, in a scope, as one change: every #111111 text colour to $color/text, every 16 font size to 18. Use find_properties first to see the values in use. Reports how many layers changed; none is not an error.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

from.description: The value to find. `#abc` matches `#AABBCC`; `$color/text` matches a use of that variable.

property.description:
The property, in the file's spelling, dotted into nested objects; lists are looked through. Examples:
`cornerRadius`, `content.size`, `fills.color`, `stroke.width`.

scope.description: Only inside this page, component or layer.

to.description: What to put instead. `$color/text` binds the variable of that name (or id).

tools.name: replace_properties

tools.description: Tell the person how the work is going: what is done and what comes next, and how many plan items are done. It changes nothing in the document. Call it between parts of a long piece of work.

done.description: How many items of the plan are done.

message.description: One or two plain sentences on what is done and what is next. Shown to the person as it is.

total.description: How many items the plan has.

tools.name: report_progress

tools.description: Draw a page or node to a PNG you can look at. It is drawn the way the editor draws it. Use it to check your work; large areas at high scale are refused, so draw one frame at a time.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

node.description: The page or node to draw.

scale.description: Pixels per canvas unit, above 0 and at most 4 (default 1).

tools.name: screenshot

tools.description: Add, change or remove variables (design tokens), as one change. A variable is matched by id or by name, so sending `color/text` again changes it. Returns the id of each by name; bind one with {"$var": id}.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

remove.description: Variables to remove, by id or name. A variable still in use cannot be removed.

variables.description:
Variables to add or change, in the file format: `{"name": "color/text", "type": "color", "values":
[{"value": "#111111"}, {"value": "#EEEEEE", "when": {"Mode": "dark"}}]}`. One with the `id` or the
`name` of an existing variable replaces it; otherwise it is new.

tools.name: set_variables

tools.description: Show the computed layout of a page or node: each node's parent and bounds in page coordinates, and the layout problems found (text overflow, clipped children, overlapping siblings, nodes outside their frame). With `problems_only`, list just the problems and the nodes they involve. Use it after a change to check the result without drawing it.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

max_nodes.description: The most nodes to list (default 300, at most 2000). Past it, `truncated` is true.

node.description: A page or node id. Defaults to the first page.

problems_only.description:
Only the nodes that have a layout problem, and the problems: text that overflows, children a frame clips,
siblings that overlap, nodes outside their frame.

tools.name: snapshot_layout

tools.description: Set properties of layers: name, size, fills, layout, text content and so on, or null to reset one. All updates apply as one change, or none do; a mistake names the update and property to fix.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

set.description:
The properties to set, in the file's spelling. `null` puts one back to its default. Children are changed
with insert_nodes, move_nodes and delete_nodes.

tools.name: update_nodes
